That if the present cold keen air continues to blow, typhoid fever will quickly disappear from Runcorn and Widnes. That there have been as many as IN patients in Widnes Fever Hospital; thereon, now only 15, awl several of these will be discharged as fully restored in the COIII,O of a day or two. That those were twelve intelligent jurymen who , had to inquire into the circumstances of death of , the unfortnnate man Mc Dermott, who was killed at Whines Foundry. That they have made themselves the laughing I stock of the townsptsiple by asking for further evi- dence of the cause of death after being told that three tons had critshed the life out of the man. That less than three tons would have sufficed to have °sent more than one jurymen to the " happy hunting grounds." That by their new hill, the Ship Canal Company are seeking to close up and entirely efface from the geography of Rtinenrn the Castle Rork road. That if the road is closed it in to be hoped the Commksinnees will sPenre some equivalent, or the ratepsvers will be shut off from the fore shore altogether. That at present there are about eight outlets from the SeWerB into the Mersey, and the ship Canal Company on their plans proposed a scheme giving only one outlet. That to the unprofessional mind this seems for From sitfficient, and a skilled engineer in the per- son of Mr. Newton. of lilsrichrster, tins been en- gaged to ir,pect Runeorn'a sewerage arrangementa. and report upon thia scheme. That it is highly probable that the ratepayers of Runcorn will be saved the expense of a contest at the'fortbcoming School Board election. That although the Chtirch party hove not yet held meetingto considerthe comprehensive resolution of the Nonconformist representatives, the leaders have had an informal chat, and the only rock noon which there is likely to be a Wit. in the thing tht. chair- mon of the Board before the Board is in existence. That with this douse of the compromise ehintin- tted there is!no doubt that Mr. Pritchard would be unanimously re-elected to the position which he. tuna tilled with to much credit to himself and to the Board. That Mr. Pritchard is the oldest member on the Board, and is entitled to the chairmanship by his long serviee and the knowledge and experience he pOPRPRSPa of the School Board work.
